frontmatter.title: Quantum walks
frontmatter.description: Explicit coined-cycle, marked-hypercube and continuous-time circuits, independent checks and conditional resource scaling.

children.value: A classical random walk adds probabilities along possible routes. A quantum walk propagates amplitudes, so routes can reinforce or cancel when they meet. A coin supplies the direction register for a discrete walk; continuous-time walks instead evolve under a graph Hamiltonian. Quantum walks are useful primitives in search, sampling and quantum simulation, but their graph access, preparation and output requirements determine an application’s cost
with an actual equality oracle and
. Their graphs, evolution and output contracts differ; the resource plots are not an equal-task advantage comparison.

Binary carry gates implement the coin-controlled cycle shifts. Small circuits are checked against independent permutation matrices and amplitude recurrences. Complete measured circuits, source code, size sweeps and conditional surface-code reports are supplied. No dense shift/evolution matrix constructs a quantum gate. The

separately checks its joint marked-state reflection, clean workspace and literal Clifford+T sequence. General graph access, other marked-search families, Szegedy walks, certified arbitrary-rotation synthesis and an integrated Lean proof remain further implementations.

uses a supplied equality mark, a binary direction coin and an explicit hypercube shift. Its default 11-wire circuit has an independent small reference and separate fixed-workload surface-code report. General graph search, multiple/application predicates and Szegedy transition-state preparation remain planned; their complexity is not inferred from either bounded walk.

The default has three position bits, one coin and four steps. The diagram shows the complete coherent evolution, including H/S coin preparation and every controlled carry, before readout. The exported measured trial appends all four final measurements.

children.value: The reports retain code distances, factory choices, source/QASM digests, serial runtime and physical-fault model scores. Peak qubits are reused across serial trials. Peak times runtime is a rectangular space-time proxy, not an occupancy integral. The

primitive QASM exports describe complete measured trials. The pinned exporter may omit an overall compiled global phase; these exports are not phase-preserving specifications for later coherent control.

, not a concrete Clifford+T sequence, approximation certificate or runtime-tail guarantee. Conditional confidence assumes its scalar bounds output-distribution variation; certified confidence remains unavailable. Physical initialization/reset timing and faults, processor routing and classical readout/control/communication latency are excluded. QDK abstracts Clifford scheduling, so the original circuit’s dependency depth is not a measured hardware schedule. These exclusions prevent calling the result a fully certified hardware implementation.

counts the complete supplied oracle, five clean work wires, coin/shift,
literal 392-T/T† lowering and every measured trial for its prescribed
four-step instance. Its surface-code rows cost 12,288 ideal frequency-estimate
preparations, separately from the ten-trial ideal at-least-one search task.
These saved results have their own output and failure budget; they do not
extend the unmarked cycle scaling table or establish a cross-method advantage.

Tests cover carries/wraparound, bit order, relative phases, all input coins, parity, decomposition, all final measurements, invalid parameters and separate generation/simulation limits. Continuous-time tests use an independent bit-flip adjacency exponential and Hamming-distance product probabilities.

No Lean proof is integrated. A linked formal library would need a reproduced theorem, its input/register assumptions and a connection to these source circuits and their lowering. The available checks are bounded numerical/functional evidence.

The cycle generator allows at most 12 position bits and 256 steps, subject to a conservative controlled-shift work guard and a 250,000-operation compiled-export cap. Temporary transpilation cost is not certified by the source guard. Actual statevector/recurrence checks stop at 12 total wires and 64 steps; dense cycle matrices stop at six position bits.
